{"round":"R1","lens":"correctness","slice":"WP-SCP-024-024B","work_package":"WP-SCP-024","verdict":"BLOCKED","new_crit_count":1,"new_maj_count":2,"new_min_count":2,"new_nit_count":2,"findings":[{"id":"R1-COR-CRIT-001","severity":"CRIT","claim":"templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl is missing the Renovate inline-comment marker present on the canonical SCP self-dogfood wrapper, making it impossible for Renovate to auto-detect and bump the SHA pin in generated adopter wrappers.","evidence":"The canonical SCP self-dogfood wrapper at .github/workflows/policy-check-wrapper.yml line 56 carries `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-` immediately before the `uses:` line. The template at templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl lines 16-17 has only `# Pin must be a 40-char SHA per WP-SCP-020 020B(v).` followed by the `uses:` line — no renovate datasource comment. A Glob for `renovate/**` in the current working tree returns no files, so no `customManagers` override in a local renovate preset can be confirmed to provide an alternative detection mechanism. The renovate.json extends `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-//renovate/default#renovate/v1.0.0` (a tagged version not present in this branch's tree), and without reading that file the absence of comment-free SHA detection cannot be ruled in.","impact":"Without the `# renovate:` comment, Renovate cannot identify the SHA pin in any adopter wrapper generated from this template and cannot issue automatic SHA-bump PRs to adopters. Every cascade adopter is structurally forced into the `onboarded-operator-bump` close-state (operator-manually bumps SHA), which (a) requires filing a `TF-024X-renovate-<slug>` tracked-forward entry for every adopter, (b) disqualifies those adopters from counting toward Threshold A until a separate real Renovate cycle subsequently runs per plan-doc §8 ('Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean'), and (c) makes invariant 8 (bake EXTENDS until at least one Renovate-issued SHA pin bump has merged + observed clean) unachievable through the scaffolder's own output alone. The entire `onboarded` close-state path and the Threshold A Renovate-cycle criterion are rendered unreachable for all 5 cohort adopters by a single missing comment line in the template.","mitigation":"Add `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-` to templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl immediately before the `uses:` line (matching the position in the canonical wrapper). The substituted output would then carry the marker, enabling Renovate auto-bumps on adopter repos that have Renovate installed. If the renovate/v1.0.0 preset already contains a `customManagers` regex entry that detects the SHA pattern in `policy-check-wrapper.yml` files without needing the inline comment, add a header comment to the template documenting this and cross-referencing the preset configuration so the relationship is explicit and auditable."},{"id":"R1-COR-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The --restore mode in scripts/enable-required-check.sh sends the GitHub GET-response format `enforce_admins` object (`{\"url\":\"...\",\"enabled\":true}`) directly to the branch-protection PUT endpoint, which documents the field as a plain boolean. This is a request-body contract violation that could cause the PUT to fail with HTTP 422 and break the <30-min rollback SLO.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh line 379-381: `printf '%s' \"$restore_before_json\" | gh api -X PUT \"repos/${restore_repo}/branches/${restore_branch}/protection\" -H \"Accept: application/vnd.github+json\" --input - >/dev/null`. The `restore_before_json` is the serialised `before` object from the pre-state JSON (line 357). The Python validation at lines 339-340 confirms the script EXPECTS this field to be an object: `if not isinstance(enforce_admins, dict) or not isinstance(enforce_admins.get('enabled'), bool)`. By contrast, the forward-mode `build_payload` at lines 450-471 uses `jq -n --argjson admins \"$ENFORCE_ADMINS\"` to supply `enforce_admins` as a plain boolean. The test suite's fake `gh` in run_restore_case (test file lines 539-550) does not validate the PUT body content, so the type mismatch cannot be caught at test time. The GitHub branch-protection PUT endpoint documents `enforce_admins` as `boolean` in its OpenAPI schema.","impact":"If the GitHub API rejects a PUT body where `enforce_admins` is an object rather than a boolean, the restore call exits non-zero and `set -euo pipefail` causes the script to terminate before emitting the markdown log block. The rollback is silent-fail: branch protection is not restored, no log entry is emitted, and the operator has no audit trail of the failed attempt. The <30-min SLO declared in plan-doc invariant 7 and ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 1 is broken precisely in the scenario where it matters most (federation-primitive defect driving urgent rollback). The real-repo round-trip evidence (restore-roundtrip-evidence.md) is not yet committed, so this defect may not have been exercised against the live API.","mitigation":"Transform the captured `before` JSON into the PUT-compatible format before issuing the restore call. Extract the boolean value from `enforce_admins.enabled`, strip the `url` sub-field, and similarly remove the `url` and `checks` sub-fields from `required_status_checks` to match the PUT schema. A jq one-liner after the Python validation can perform the transformation: `restore_put_json=$(printf '%s' \"$restore_before_json\" | jq '(.enforce_admins) |= .enabled | if .required_status_checks != null then (.required_status_checks) |= del(.url, .checks) else . end')` and use `restore_put_json` instead of `restore_before_json` for the PUT call."},{"id":"R1-COR-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The test suite for check-invocation-log-entry.sh has no negative test case for `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` with an unmodified branch-protection log. All five operator-bump test cases (4-8) have the log modified; the first guard (`branch_log_modified == 1`) is never exercised in the failing direction for this cascade-status value.","evidence":"tests/check_invocation_log/test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh cases 4-8 (lines 249-360): case 4 is the happy path with a modified log; cases 5-8 each write to `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md` before committing, so `branch_log_modified=1` in all five. check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 182: `[ \"$branch_log_modified\" -eq 1 ] || die \"ERROR: branch-protection-log.md was not modified for cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump\"` is the first guard in the `onboarded-operator-bump` path. No test exercises the path where this guard fires. For comparison, the analogous negative test for `onboarded` exists (case 2, lines 218-225) and the analogous negative test for `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` (log IS modified when it should not be) exists as case 10 (lines 372-391).","impact":"A future refactor that accidentally removes or inverts the `branch_log_modified` guard for the `onboarded-operator-bump` path would pass all existing tests. An operator could file `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` with a valid STATUS.md TF row but without actually running `enable-required-check.sh`, and CI would pass. This undermines the audit-trail invariant (plan-doc invariant 2: 'Required-check enablement is operator-run + invocation-logged + CI-enforced') for the operator-bump path, which is already the higher-risk path (Renovate is disabled; operator is the sole actor).","mitigation":"Add a test case: init_case_repo, write DISPATCH-NOTE with `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` and a valid `- **Target:**` line, write STATUS.md with a regex-passing TF row, do NOT modify branch-protection-log.md (leave it empty as committed by init_case_repo), commit, run_case expecting exit 1 with stderr containing 'ERROR: branch-protection-log.md was not modified for cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump'."},{"id":"R1-COR-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"The DISPATCH-NOTE scope table documents substitution placeholder names in lowercase (`{{default-branch}}`, `{{scp-sha}}`, `{{scorecard-emit}}`), but the template and sed invocations use UPPERCASE (`{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}`, `{{SCP_SHA}}`, `{{SCORECARD_EMIT}}`). The implementation is internally consistent; the DISPATCH-NOTE documentation is incorrect.","evidence":"DISPATCH-NOTE line 31: `Substitutions: {{default-branch}}, {{scp-sha}}, {{scorecard-emit}}`. templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl lines 6, 17, 19: `{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}`, `{{SCP_SHA}}`, `{{SCORECARD_EMIT}}`. scripts/scaffold-downstream.sh lines 157-161: sed expressions `s/{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}/.../g`, `s/{{SCP_SHA}}/.../g`, `s/{{SCORECARD_EMIT}}/.../g` all use uppercase.","impact":"An operator or cascade-slice author who consults the DISPATCH-NOTE to understand the substitution contract (e.g., when manually patching a generated wrapper or verifying template output) would use incorrect placeholder names. Could mislead downstream documentation for 024C-F slice authors who copy the DISPATCH-NOTE pattern.","mitigation":"Correct the DISPATCH-NOTE scope table entry for the adopter wrapper template row to use UPPERCASE placeholder names: `{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}`, `{{SCP_SHA}}`, `{{SCORECARD_EMIT}}`."},{"id":"R1-COR-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"The forward-mode prior-green-CI safety check in enable-required-check.sh queries workflow runs without filtering by branch, allowing a successful run on any PR branch to satisfy a check that is described as requiring green CI 'on the default branch' in plan-doc §5.4.","evidence":"scripts/enable-required-check.sh lines 261-269: `gh api \"repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?workflow_id=${WORKFLOW_ID}&status=success&created>=${prior_green_cutoff}\"`. The `$BRANCH` variable (parsed from `--branch` argument at line 169) is available but not appended as `&branch=${BRANCH}`. The DISPATCH-NOTE scope table entry for `--restore` mode states the safety check is 'refuses forward-mode invocation against repo with no successful policy-check / scp/policy-check run on default branch in last 60 days'.","impact":"The safety check could be satisfied by a green run on a stale PR branch that was later reverted, allowing `enable-required-check.sh` to proceed even if the adopter's wrapper has never successfully run on their actual default branch. The foot-gun the safety check is meant to close (enabling the required-check before the wrapper is confirmed working on the branch it protects) remains partially open.","mitigation":"Append `&branch=${BRANCH}` to the workflow runs API query: `gh api \"repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?workflow_id=${WORKFLOW_ID}&status=success&created>=${prior_green_cutoff}&branch=${BRANCH}\"`."},{"id":"R1-COR-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"scripts/scaffold-downstream.sh line 163 calls `mkdir -p \"${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github\"` redundantly after line 150 already creates `${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github/workflows` via `mkdir -p \"$WORKFLOWS_DIR\"`, which implicitly creates the `.github` intermediate directory.","evidence":"scripts/scaffold-downstream.sh line 149: `WORKFLOWS_DIR=\"${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github/workflows\"`. Line 150: `mkdir -p \"$WORKFLOWS_DIR\"` — creates `.github` as an intermediate directory. Line 163: `mkdir -p \"${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github\"` — no-op since `.github` already exists.","impact":"No functional impact; `mkdir -p` on an existing directory is idempotent. Cosmetic redundancy.","mitigation":"Remove line 163 (`mkdir -p \"${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github\"`)."},{"id":"R1-COR-nit-002","severity":"nit","claim":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh constructs slug-specific regex patterns (`TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}...`) rather than embedding the plan-doc §2 invariant 2 literal regex byte-for-byte. While the deviation is deliberately stricter (prevents cross-adopter contamination), it creates silent drift risk if the plan-doc regex evolves.","evidence":"scripts/check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 192-194: `pattern = rf'TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\\): \\S.{{19,}}'`. Plan-doc §2 invariant 2 literal: `TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\\): \\S.{19,}`. The `(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` segment is replaced by the literal slug, meaning the status-enum set and description-length requirement are the only parts shared verbatim.","impact":"If the plan-doc regex is updated (e.g., adding a new status value like `in-review` to the enum, or adjusting the slug character set), the script must be manually updated in parallel. The relationship between plan-doc spec and implementation is undocumented inline.","mitigation":"Add an inline comment citing the plan-doc §2 invariant 2 generic regex and explaining the deliberate slug-specific substitution: `# Plan-doc §2 invariant 2 generic regex: TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+... # Slug-specific pattern used here to prevent cross-adopter contamination.`"}]}
